title: The mindful will be among real shades and springs.
subtitle: The opposite of the smoke

row.title: the mindful
sub: did the duties, left the forbidden

then: Ibn Kathir says the people of taqwa are those who {idea}worship Him by doing the obligations and leaving the forbidden.{/idea} They will be {reward}in gardens and springs, the opposite of the wretched under black smoke.{/reward}
now: A hot afternoon, and you find a tree with deep shade and a water fountain next to it. Pure relief. {reward}That is the picture, made eternal.{/reward} It is built from ordinary daily choices.
old: Taqwa sounds like something only for very religious people.
new: Taqwa is doing what is asked and leaving what is forbidden, one day at a time.
try: Leave one small forbidden thing today, quietly, for Allah.

title: And whatever fruit they desire.
subtitle: Their wish is answered
then: Ibn Kathir says {reward}from every kind of fruit, they will have whatever they request.{/reward} The ones who held back their desires for Allah {idea}now have their desires met.{/idea}
now: You walk past the bakery while fasting. You skip the second helping so you can give some away. {reward}Every desire you set aside for Allah is waiting for you, answered.{/reward}
old: Holding back my desires means losing them.
new: What I hold back for Allah, He gives back in full.
try: Pick one craving today and give it up for Allah's sake.

title: Eat and drink happily, for what you used to do.
subtitle: Spoken to them with kindness
then: Ibn Kathir says {reward}this will be said to them out of kindness.{/reward} The deniers were told "go to what you denied." {idea}The mindful are told "eat and drink, for what you used to do."{/idea}
now: You come home after a long shift and someone has dinner ready, and says: sit, you earned this. {reward}Imagine Allah saying that to you.{/reward}
old: My small good deeds will be forgotten.
new: Allah will welcome me with kindness for what I used to do.
try: Do one good deed today you would love to hear mentioned that Day.

title: This is how We reward those who do good.
subtitle: A rule, not a one-off
then: Ibn Kathir says this restates the point: {reward}this is Our reward for whoever does good.{/reward} Earlier the surah said {trap}thus do We deal with the criminals.{/trap} {idea}Both are rules. Both are fair.{/idea}
now: You wonder if your effort at being good is noticed: patience with your kids, honesty at work, the extra mile for a neighbor. {reward}This is the rule: it is rewarded, every time.{/reward}
old: Being good does not really pay off.
new: Allah has a rule: those who do good are rewarded like this.
try: Do something today with excellence, not just enough.

title: Woe, that Day, to the deniers who missed all this.
subtitle: Eighth refrain: after the reward of the good
then: This refrain comes right after {reward}the reward of the good: shade, springs, fruit, a kind welcome.{/reward} {idea}Here the woe is about what the deniers gave up.{/idea} Ibn Kathir notes the mindful are in the opposite state of the wretched.
now: A friend offers you a seat on a trip of a lifetime and you say no because you could not be bothered. Later you see the photos. {idea}This woe is for missing what was offered.{/idea}
old: Denying the Day only costs me if the Fire is real.
new: Denial also costs me the Garden that was offered to me.
try: Think of the Garden for one minute today, and say: O Allah, I want it.

title: Eat and enjoy a little. You are criminals.
subtitle: A short enjoyment, then the end
then: Ibn Kathir says this is addressed to the deniers as {trap}a command of threat{/trap}: enjoy yourselves {trap}for a short, small, brief time.{/trap} He compares it to "We let them enjoy a little, then drive them to a severe punishment."
now: Friday night, takeaway, a new show, no thought of tomorrow. Nothing wrong with the food. {idea}The question is whether "a little while" is all you are living for.{/idea}
old: Life is for enjoying now. Worry about later, later.
new: Enjoyment here is short. I want it to lead somewhere lasting.
try: Before your next meal, say Bismillah and thank Allah after.

title: Woe, that Day, to the deniers who chose the little.
subtitle: Ninth refrain: after the short enjoyment
then: This refrain follows {trap}"eat and enjoy a little, you are criminals."{/trap} Ibn Kathir says after the little while {trap}they will be driven to the Fire already mentioned.{/trap} {idea}The woe is for trading forever for a little.{/idea}
now: You spend your best years on things that will not matter in a decade: the grudges, the status games, the endless scroll. {idea}A little, for a lot.{/idea}
old: A little fun now is worth the risk.
new: Trading forever for a little is the worst deal there is.
try: Give ten minutes today that you would have spent scrolling to something for the Hereafter.

title: When told to bow, they do not bow.
subtitle: Pride that will not bend
then: Ibn Kathir says when they {idea}were ordered to pray with the believers{/idea}, {trap}they refused and turned away arrogantly.{/trap} Of all their actions, the surah names this one at the end: {idea}not bowing.{/idea}
now: The adhan goes off on your phone during a meeting. You swipe it away. Not because you are against prayer, just because bowing right now feels awkward. {idea}Notice what is really stopping you.{/idea}
old: Missing a prayer is just about being busy.
new: Sometimes what stops me bowing is a little pride. Bowing breaks it.
try: Pray your next prayer on time, even if it is a little awkward where you are.

title: Woe, that Day, to the deniers who would not bow.
subtitle: Tenth refrain: after refusing to pray

row.title: a head that will not bow

then: This is the last of the ten refrains. It comes after {trap}"when told to bow, they do not bow."{/trap} Ibn Kathir says they {trap}refused arrogantly.{/trap} {idea}Denial is not only a belief. It shows up as a refusal to bow.{/idea}
now: You believe in the Day. You would never deny it. But when the time for prayer comes, your body says no. {idea}The verse asks what your actions are saying.{/idea}
old: As long as I believe, not praying is a small thing.
new: A head that will not bow is a kind of denial too. I want mine to bow.
try: Make one sujud today a little longer and ask Allah for steadiness.

title: After this, what words will they ever believe?
subtitle: If not the Quran, then what?
then: Ibn Kathir says: {trap}if they do not believe in this Quran, what talk will they believe in?{/trap} He links it to the verse asking what speech after Allah and His signs they will believe. {idea}The surah has given everything; there is nothing after it.{/idea}
now: You keep waiting for the perfect lecture, the perfect video, the moment that will finally change you. {idea}The words are already here, in your hands.{/idea}
old: I will change when I hear something powerful enough.
new: Nothing will be more powerful than the Quran. It is already here.
try: Read this whole surah once this week, slowly, start to finish.
